Date: 2027-04-18
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM), Tom Alvarez (CTO, Horizon Health), Sara Lin (Head of AI), Nina Park (Security Lead), Alex Monroe (DevOps)
summary: Kickoff for Horizon Health onboarding to Redwood Inference. Covered scope, success criteria, security requirements, deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and next steps. Agreed to share SSO/SAML and SOC2 docs, schedule infra deep dive, and deliver dedicated sizing proposal.
topics: Deployment options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
Traffic profiling, batching and cost considerations
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, uh, Horizon Health onboarding with Redwood. I'm Maya, AE, and with me are Diego, our SE, and Priya who will lead the onboarding.
[00:14] Tom Alvarez: Great, thanks Maya. Tom here. Quick note we have a hard deadline end of Q2 to be live with a pilot so, uh, roughly six weeks.
[00:24] Priya Patel: Thanks Tom, got it. We'll aim for that, we'll draft a timeline after this call.
[00:30] Sara Lin: Hi, Sara. We're most focused on inference latency for user-facing triage and also strict data residency, we can't send PHI out to third party, so private or VPC looks likely.
[00:44] Diego Ramos: Understood. We support Private deployments and VPC connectors, we also have Dedicated reserved pools if you want managed infra in a customer-dedicated tenant. Both can integrate with your KMS.
[00:56] Nina Park: Nina here, security lead. Two things: SSO with SCIM/SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration plus incoming egress restrictions. Do you have SOC2 cert and penetration test reports?
[01:12] Maya Chen: Yes, we do. I'll share the SOC2 report and our security FAQ. Also we have an architecture doc for KMS integration — we'll include that.
[01:20] Alex Monroe: Quick ops question, what about network egress — can we lock down outbound to our VPC?
[01:27] Diego Ramos: For Private we deploy into your VPC or your on-prem, so traffic stays inside. For Dedicated, we offer customer-dedicated GPU pools in our infra with VPC peering and strict network policies. There are tradeoffs on operational overhead and latency.
[01:43] Tom Alvarez: Can you run benchmarks? We want to compare to our in-house self-host setup for cost and latency.
[01:50] Diego Ramos: Absolutely. We can run a benchmarking pilot — we'll need your sample payloads and traffic profile. Our bench will measure tail latency and token cost across model variants and quantization.
[02:02] Sara Lin: Model question: are you supporting the Llama-3 family and runtimes for quantized tables?
[02:08] Diego Ramos: Yes, Llama-3 variants are in our catalog; we do kernel selection and quantization-friendly paths, but some names get garbled in transcripts — you might see 'Llama three' or 'lama-three' in some docs. We also support seamless fallback to smaller variants to meet SLOs.
[02:26] Nina Park: How do you handle logs and retention, especially for PHI? We need audit trails but also the option to disable retention.
[02:34] Maya Chen: We have configurable retention and options to disable PII logging. For Private you can opt to keep logs within your environment. We'll include the logging controls in the security pack.
[02:45] Tom Alvarez: Timeline — what does a six-week pilot look like?
[02:49] Priya Patel: Typical onboarding: week 1-2 infra setup + SSO, week 2-3 ingest/testing and benchmarks, week 4 small pilot with live traffic, week 5 acceptance and tuning, week 6 handover and runbook. We can compress if needed.
[03:05] Alex Monroe: For infra we'll need a runbook for Dedicated sizing; our traffic is bursty with 95th percentile spikes to 400 rps and average around 60 rps, median sequence length 120 tokens, 90th 450 tokens.
[03:20] Diego Ramos: That's helpful. For those numbers I'd recommend starting with 4 GPU nodes in a dedicated pool and we can auto-scale for bursts; I'll put together sizing based on exact model choice.
[03:33] Sara Lin: Cost control is important — can we set batch sizes and prefix caching?
[03:38] Diego Ramos: Yes, Redwood has batching and KV cache/prefix caching. We'll propose cache strategies; note that caching benefits are workload dependent — if your requests are highly unique, caching helps less. Also quantization affects throughput and fidelity, we'll propose profiles.
[03:55] Tom Alvarez: Any blockers on SSO? We use Okta.
[03:59] Maya Chen: Okta is widely supported. We'll send the SAML and SCIM integration guide and our sample metadata.
[04:06] Nina Park: About compliance docs, can you provide SOC2, pen test high level, and data processing addendum?
[04:12] Maya Chen: Yes. I'll attach SOC2 and the DPA; pen test summary we'll include, full reports require an NDA but we'll start with the summary.
[04:23] Priya Patel: I'll create the onboarding checklist and invite calendar events for the infra deep dive and weekly check-ins.
[04:29] Tom Alvarez: For the bench, how long to get results?
[04:32] Diego Ramos: Once we have sample traffic and access (or payloads), we can run an initial bench in 5-7 business days; full end-to-end with multiple model variants ~2 weeks.
[04:42] Sara Lin: Are there any known issues with our stack? We're running Kubernetes on AWS EKS, and some parts are behind private subnets.
[04:49] Diego Ramos: EKS is common. For Private deployments we can work with your networking team to either do VPC peering or run the private control plane. We'll document the exact port requirements in the runbook.
[05:00] Alex Monroe: Will you need keys to our KMS?
[05:03] Maya Chen: We integrate with customer KMS through delegated access; we don't persist keys. We'll document the flow.
[05:09] Tom Alvarez: Competitive note: we're also talking to Anthropic and exploring an in-house self-host. We'll weigh cost and latency and operational burden.
[05:18] Maya Chen: Totally fair — we'll try to make the dedicated proposal show TCO and latency tradeoffs side-by-side.
[05:24] Priya Patel: Ok, to recap next steps: Maya will share security docs and SOC2, Diego will produce sizing and bench plan once payloads are provided, Priya will share onboarding timeline and calendar invites, Horizon will provide traffic sample and Okta admin contact.
[05:38] Sara Lin: Sounds good. Also please include a short note on rollback/fallback behavior if a model upgrade regresses quality.
[05:45] Diego Ramos: We'll include canary and automatic fallback policies and the eval harness used for quality checks.
[05:52] Tom Alvarez: Thanks everyone. We'll wait for the docs and schedule the infra deep dive.
[05:58] Maya Chen: Great, thanks all, we'll follow up by email and I'll upload the docs to the shared drive.
[06:04] (crosstalk) Nina Park: Thanks.
[06:06] End of recording

Notes: Transcript has occasional recognition issues (product names, acronyms). References: security pack link (sent after call), onboarding checklist (Priya will share), benchmark spreadsheet (Diego).
